utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Milosevic, you've got this session for your cross-examination. We'll have in mind we'll starting rather late, and of course that time will be added to it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Milosevic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. De la Brosse, in paragraph 61, page 60, paragraph 2 of your report, speaking about reporting from Vukovar and the testimony of civilians, you criticise the fact that the testimony was never firsthand. And I'm quoting you there. In paragraph 59, page 57, at the end of the first paragraph, you say that contrary to professional ethics, the reporters show as witnesses people who were either too close to the events -- were persons who were either too close to the events they were reporting on or too far away from them. And in paragraph 5 on page 187, speaking about the possibility of foreign journalists reporting from Kosovo and Metohija there was only secondhand information to be had which included the risk of error and imprecision. My question to you is this: You, therefore, indirect informing -- you considered this to be unreliable, isn't that so? You consider that that should not be something that should be resorted to because there's always the risk of error. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In -- generally speaking, a journalist reporting looks for direct witnesses of events, firsthand witnesses, whatever the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So not only the fact that you don't speak Serbian, but from the entire contents of your report, it would emerge that you base your analyses on other people's text, other people's articles and books which speak about the state of affairs of media -- of the media in Yugoslavia and Serbia, and you state that in your footnotes and not with a direct access to the situation. So how come something you criticise in others, that is to say, indirect information, you consider to be allowed when you yourself are in question. Why are you an exception to that rule?

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The work that I based my report on is to go to the source, source information, of course. And let me go back to that in a minute. And these were established on the basis of academic articles, press articles, and reports by people who were in the field, on the ground. And also I met a -- I had a number of meetings with research journalists who were on the spot. So I think that the scope is fairly broad. The samples that I took were very broad from my point of view.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you're talking about sources, I asked you towards the end of the last session what your sources were, in fact, and you indicated tab 3 to me. And that is a fairly short document. It is three pages long, and you have academic works, books and articles, in fact, and then again you have analytical books and articles, and then you have some other articles and agencies and reports by different organisations, and finally, interviews with different journalists, conversations with them and so on. So am I right if I conclude that you did not report on the state of the media because you weren't able to follow the media yourself, but you speak about that on the basis of what your sources think about those media, and in that regard it is quite obviously that this was done on a selective basis; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: An impression as to the goal that my report had, as I said last week, the object of my report was to describe the mechanisms of propaganda in play in the Serbian press. And this work was based on the sources, the sources that I quoted. Of course, these are not all the sources that I used. This is not an exhaustive list in document number 3. But on the other hand, this work of mine is also based on questionnaires and sounding performed together with the team that I work with in Belgrade. And for its part, the team used -- made use not only of the press but also a good knowledge of the situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In order to round off this subject matter, we can see that you used, on a selective basis, certain sources which you considered in one way or another can serve your purpose to construe your findings. However, there is no doubt that you did not conduct an analysis, perform an analysis of the press in Yugoslavia and Serbia at all; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sources that were used to accomplish this work and compile this report, which is my work, is the fruit of my own personal work, and as I said, the team on the spot in Belgrade. The selection of sources that was made was made on the basis of the representative samples that we were able to find at the time quoted by the Serbian press. So they were extracts from the Serbian press. And this was the core of the knowledge. It is not exhaustive, but nevertheless, it helps us in representing the type of situation that we found when we went to Belgrade to study the press and television as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. De la Brosse. Now, on the basis of what criteria were you able to conclude that this was a representative sample at all? How do you come to that conclusion? Because we noted that you weren't able to read through the press clippings yourself or analyse them yourself. You used intermediaries and intermediary sources. So why is this a representative sample except for you want to represent it being as such?

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bulk of the subject matter that was studied, as I said last week, represents about 20 million documents that were examined and processed - 20.000 documents, I'm sorry - which were examined and research by journalists from Belgrade. Of course, these 20.000 pages were not the total of everything that the press in Belgrade put out, but at least the researchers and journalists that studied those texts were able to select a number of them, a number of articles in which we could see effects of propaganda.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, all right, Mr. de la Brosse. From this vast bulk of material, and you say that they made the selection and everything -- everybody can select what they like according to their motives, so this body of material, you have just shown certain extracts of my speeches here, one speech in which I say that there is terrorism in Kosovo and the right to self-defence, which I state now -- here and now again. There is terrorism in Kosovo, and people do have the right to defend themselves. So is that all that you were able to extract from that whole body of material as some kind of illustration to bear out your assertion that the press was motivated by this and diffused negative sentiments?

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you be more specific in your question, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I said from this whole body of material that you say you looked through, and we just saw a brief excerpt from my speech to the Assembly where I say that there is terrorism over Kosovo, and I speak of the right to self-defence and self-protection which is what I say today. So I don't see that anything should be changed. Where do you see propaganda here in the impassioned press? Perhaps there wasn't -- Do you want to say that there was no terrorism in Kosovo and I just invented it, or somebody challenged the right to defence from terrorism?

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to take up a position with respect to the bases and foundations of that alone, but what I would like to say in quoting the excerpt, you yourself in your speech used terminology which could be qualified as being terminology used by the media wishing to present in a pejorative way and stigmatising one specific community. In this particular case it was the Albanians of Kosovo and by the same token the Croatian community as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I thoughts we cleared that up. No mention is made of the either of the Croatian or Albanian community anywhere but what I was talking about was Albanian terrorists and extremists, extremists in Croatia who committed crimes, who had already committed crimes at the time against Serbs in Croatia. So why do you equate extremists all the time and the nationalities that those extremists belong to? Terrorism knows no national ethnic boundaries. A killer is a killer, regardless of the ethnic group or nation he belongs to. So why do you keep saying that we're stigmatising a national community, an ethnic community because certain terrorists are by virtue of their ethnicity, something that they are intrinsically. You won't be able to find that anywhere. Find me an example, if you can, where I or anybody speaks about Croats or Albanians as criminals? On the contrary, we're just talking about extremists. Is that quite clear or not from what you were able to read?

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I tried to explain through my report, as I said last week with respect to the -- is that the media used terminology or a vocabulary with a view to stigmatising or creating stereotypes with respect to one or another community, one or another ethnic group, and what I wanted to say, with respect to the example to what you've just quoted, is that throughout the speech in question, you yourself took part in disseminating these stereotypes. Now, if we wish to know whether the Albanians in Kosovo ran any risk or not, I can't really say because it's not the subject of my report. And let me remind you that I was describing the propaganda mechanism, and also that there was part of the report concerning the results of the collective research and sources of the Belgrade team. So this report was compiled - how shall I put this? - in the space of one month. That was the time span given the object and time that I had at my disposal as I underlined last time. It was impossible for me and that the three-member team that I had in Belgrade to look at the entire body of material that existed. And ideally, this would -- should have been analysed, all of it, in an exhaustive fashion. So the part of the media in the diffusion of stereotypes. Now I think that I can say, looking at the material I had access to and by analysing the propaganda mechanisms in the Serbian press, I think I'll be -- can say although I'm aware of the facts that it is not an exhaustive source matter, that they did take part in diffusing stereotypes, in putting out stereotypes, in propagating messages, ethnically coloured, of hatred. And this was true manipulation in actual fact, and the instrumentalisation of the political times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that would be correct if what you said a moment ago were correct, that it is claimed that the Albanians from Kosovo represent a terrorist movement. And that was never stated anywhere. What was stated was that they were terrorists, not Albanians. Mention was not made of Albanians. The reference was to terrorists, not the ethnic Albanian community at all, which you in fact should know full well. This is reversal of thesis as it's called. Do you really think that as a scientist you have the right to reverse the thesis in this way?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think you've made this point and we cannot go any further into it. The witness has given the answer which he has. It will be a matter for us to judge. Shall we move on to a different point?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in compiling your expert report as an expert, let me ask you this: Do you -- I don't suppose you think that you should use sources that are not characterised by neutrality, or rather, let me put it in this way: Do you think that sources should be used which are neutral sources, that is to say, sources which are objective and not coloured and impassioned in any way?

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one has to know what the purpose is and to see whether it's objective or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the purpose of objectivity is to ascertain the truth, as far as I'm able to understand it. Do you consider that for an expert report a relevant sources texts from the titles of which one would see hatred on the part of their authors, hatred towards the Serb people, towards myself personally, and so on? Let me read out a few titles of the texts you used by way of example, and you quote them in your footnotes. For example, footnote 87 on page 42: Jean-Paul Collette is the author of the article and it is titled "Opportunistic Monster" in the daily, Le Soir. And part of the article says that Slobodan Milosevic, according to much testimony, himself provided inspiration for propaganda messages on television through which he disseminating his nationalistic hysteria. Do you have any illustrations of the dissemination of nationalistic hysteria from my speeches at all? And this very biased text, can it be the basis for any kind of expert report at all along your lines?

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you tell me exactly where that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I've already told you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's paragraph 45.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Footnote 87.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Paragraph 45.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there in fact I did base myself on an article by a journalist from Le Soir. It's one of the main newspapers in Belgium, that is in French-speaking Belgium. This is the testimony of a journalist who was on site. The testimony talks about the -- Milosevic's control over the contents of the press, and it is confirmed, and I quote the Borisav Jovic, one of his closest collaborators, Borisav Jovic, that is, and every day he would write, as of 1990 that Slobodan Milosevic inspired or, rather, put out three articles that -- that he was asked to write in Politika and in which he attacks directly the Federal Prime Minister, Mr. Ante Markovic. What I'm saying is that I relied both on the journalists from Le Soir, Jean-Paul Collette, but also on Borisav Jovic's testimony. And I could also quote the excerpt that we saw already, the clip, the -- from Dusan Mitevic who was the director of RTS and who emphasised that Milosevic had direct responsibility as regards distribution of false information and reporting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just don't know which false report he mentioned, because you keep confusing things. But let me give you a few more examples. I asked you a question of principle, a general question. Is it possible to use articles and consider them to be objective when at first glance already they're inflammatory and biased? On page 82, you refer to a text from the Internet, also Benedicte Chesnelong, and the title is "Serbia, the Black Hole of the Balkans." And the author obviously had a fine opinion of Serbia. That title in itself surely disqualifies the text as a source of information for what should be a scientific study.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you. You characterise the witness's response as not being an answer to the question. His response was that he relied on the matter you quoted, but he also relied on other matter. So in fact, it was a response. Now, moving on to this question. Page 82. We'll see if we can find the reference. I certainly remember the reference. I don't remember it being on page 82.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's footnote 208, "Serbia, the Black Hole of the Balkans" is the title. The very title disqualifies such an article as a source of information for a scientific study.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Surely you would agree with that, Mr. de la Brosse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's deal with that. It is in fact page 84 of ours, but it is footnote 208. Yes, Mr. de la Brosse, if you've found that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's at the end of the paragraph 90.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The source in question here is a mission report from the International Human Rights Federation which went on site from the 19th to the 22nd of September, 1997. The report was prepared by a member of the International Human Rights Federation, and this is a source which in my mind was objective. Was I right? Was I wrong? I allow the Judges to come to that decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the whole point, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let him finish.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One clarification about the title of an article or a report. The operating internal mechanisms for the press mean that the newspapers in particular were accustomed to choose headlines that would catch people's attention and which did not really reflect the contents. That is the idea that was being put forward by the headlines. So I don't think one should only base oneself on the headline or the title of an article in order to judge its content and then to disqualify it. The article -- the article has to be judged on its own merit and the facts it contains.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Very well, Mr. de la Brosse. Now, please look at footnote 81. Here you have Ms. Florence Hartmann who is an employee here in this illegal Tribunal who wrote a book, "Milosevic, a Diagonal of a Madman". Isn't such hatred sufficient basis to doubt the objectivity of such a source? If the other side doesn't believe that one who openly expresses hatred towards me and the Serbian people could be exempted from any participation in legal proceedings. You see, the things you use. You're using senseless propaganda that for a whole decade demonised the Serb people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness answer on the specific point, and we'll have a translation, if we may, from the French of footnote 81, "Milosevic, la diagonale du fou".

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: This is the diagonal of the fou, of the madman. It also refers to the chess player, to the bishop that goes diagonally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you feel that is rather inflammatory and full of hatred to be able to be used as an objective source for any judgement on your part?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness answer. The translation we got was that it was the diagonal of the madman and also a reference to the bishop in chess, which moves diagonally, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. That is the interpretation that I made of the book which directly refers to chess. A few words about the source that you're criticising me for having quoted. The journalist who wrote the book was a journalist from Le Monde, the daily newspaper Le Monde and was who was a correspondent in Belgrade for several years for that newspaper. She is -- she's a journalist who speaks Serbo-Croat, and she heard and she saw many things which happened at the time in Serbia. I didn't make any value judgement on the work. What I simply say is that she is a journalist who is respected for her work. The book on which I partially based myself contains some information which was collected, which was gleaned in Serbia throughout the first half of the decade of the 1990s -- decade of the 1990s. It appeared in 1999, and it is the work of -- former work, work that she had been doing before. If that journalist changed her activities, that change happened subsequent to the book, and I used it as the testimony of the journalist who was in Belgrade in Serbia until, I think, 1995 or 1996, if I'm not mistaken. It has to be checked, but I believe that she -- that the work that you're referring to came -- that she does now, the work she's doing now is after the book was published.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. de la Brosse. You are clearly selectively using your sources. And, of course, they are indirect sources. Tell me, on page 18 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness deal with that assertion, you see. If you make assertions like that, the witness must have the chance to deal with it. The point has been made before but you can give us your answer now it's made so plainly. The accusation is that you were purely selective in the sources you chose to support your thesis, and it must follow from that that you ignored sources which might have been to the contrary. Now, that is the characterisation which is made of your evidence and your report. You should have the opportunity to deal with it and tell us whether it's an accurate characterisation or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I worked on sources which I believed Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. were objective, sources which from my point of view varied. This is in my own point of view. I worked on many reports from very different types of organisations. They might be French-speaking organisations or English-speaking organisations or other languages. Any way, organisations whose objective in general was to protect human rights and the freedom of the press. I worked on official reports from the United Nations, from the Council of Europe, and so I think that I had access to different types of sources which were objective.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But obviously you did not analyse at all the contents of the Serbian and Yugoslav media, but you are now yourself confirming that you used selectively a certain number of books which fitted into this order that you had received from the opposing side as you wrote on the cover page of your work at the request of the Prosecution, as you yourself said. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness answer that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The sources with which I worked, let me repeat, were in part provided by the Belgrade team. I'm referring particularly to the press articles. The sources on which I worked in the report are ones which I found myself. Let me remind you, I began to become interested in the issue of propaganda spread by the media of the former Yugoslavia as of 1994, and in the work that I worked for a report is without [no translation] -- Clips, television clips. How should I say this? The sources are not only sources that I got from the Belgrade team.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. They are the fruit of the work of this entire machinery and propaganda that I would call global propaganda that has been satanising the Serbs for more than a decade. Are you aware of that or not? Demonising the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can't answer that question. Did you perhaps watch the CNN last night, for instance? There's an example how low such propaganda can fall. They were interviewing a journalist who never interviewed me and who ranks me among some sort of dictators, even though we had free elections in Serbia every two years. And who, among various arguments mentions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's see if the witness saw the programme. Were you watching CNN last night, Mr. de la Brosse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I wasn't watching -- I didn't watch television last night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And among all the different arguments that he chose as this was just an excerpt --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. It's no good asking him about television last night. Now, move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, I was saying that when arguments are so thin and untenable, then people are prone to resort to such very base propaganda which reveals that you're having a lot of problems with the real facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the witness has answered the question on these matters. Have you got anything more specific to ask? And I have in mind that the witness should have the opportunity to deal with the various documents which you produced. When we find a convenient time, he can deal with those.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know when we'll find any convenient time, Mr. May. As far as I'm concerned, it suits me that he referred to whatever you like if there is enough time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But among the various things attributed to me, the one mentioned yesterday, the only one mentioned yesterday was that my wife said I was handsome.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. May. Talking about my wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nice placed under the ELMO here a specific paragraph from tab number 6. This is the last paragraph, and it relates to verbal attacks on the so-called independent media, and in brackets, quotations. And I've highlighted that paragraph in the same way as it was highlighted on the screen here, and it says as follows: [In English] "Published by political on 29th of March, 1996, Mira Markovic," - that is my wife --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What number is it? What number paragraph?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is -- I don't have the number of the paragraph here. It is tab 6 and on page 1 of that document in tab 6 and at the bottom of the page. We all saw this on the screen. It was selected as something meant to be extremely important. Have you found it? [In English] "In an interview published by Politika on 29th of March, 1996, Mira Markovic," [Interpretation] that is my wife, [In English] "referred to the independent media as," [Interpretation] and then she is quoted as saying, [In English] "Stirring up political and nationalistic hatred, defeatism and physical violence directed against men." End of quotation. And it says that it was quoted by Reporters Without Borders in "La liberte de la presse," Le Monde, 1997, et cetera. And since I have found the original text, all of them having been published by her, this paragraph from which this was extracted relates to something quite different, and I will read to you the paragraph since it says here, speaking about the independent media which is not true, and the paragraph reads as follows: "Such politically profiled, morally and intellectually intoned rightists," she's talking about the right wing, "can hardly become a political subject in the changes which are historically justified by their method and content and outcome. By their current political, moral and intellectual being, the right wing in Serbia, judging at least by the press that supports it, can only be the vehicle of cheap nihilism, very rudeness, extreme rudeness, national, religious and political hatred, destructive defeatism, physical and political violence over people, the product of a new Balkan Fascism." So this is a pure forgery because it doesn't relate to any independent media at all. Secondly, it is taken out of context and quoted only half of the sentence. And number three, Mr. de la Brosse, when Mr. le Pen won a large percentage of votes in the elections, the whole of France got on its feet to demand and to wonder what such support to the right wing meant. So this is a text written by her about the right wing, not about the media.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, let the witness have a chance to answer -- wait a moment. Wait a moment. Let the witness -- let him answer. What is said about this passage, Mr. De la Brosse, is that it is a passage which is taken out of context and that the writer was referring essentially to something else. Now, can you help us about that or not? Can you say anything more about it than what's written on the exhibit which we have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I say in the footnote, that quotation that I relied on comes from Reporters Without Borders, about freedom in press in the field -- in the world. I used in good faith the information which is found in the report. Obviously wrongly so. I think it's an error that was made by the team that was -- that was responsible for drafting that part of the report in the former Yugoslavia. But I replaced that comment into the context of other statements in respect of the report in question, that is the preceding report or those that are found on page 2, which is not a direct quotation of Mrs. Markovic but is a resolution of the party that she was leader of, and they are attacks on the independent press which is characterised as mercenary, as people who denounce others as traitors. So if that quotation comes -- is taken out of context and is incorrect, I apologise, but it has to be put back into a context of other statements by Mira Markovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let him finish.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In newspapers like Duga or quoted in the report of the International Committee for Independent Press in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, which is on page -- from 2 to 7 of the list. Page 2, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let us not waste any more time. Luckily Mira Markovic -- whatever Mira Markovic wrote has been published and published at the time she wrote it, so that forgeries are impossible, regardless of the intentions of those behind it. But let us move on to the next point. In -- I have to leave out some things because time is flying. In footnote 44, page 22, in the second paragraph of that footnote or, rather, in the third, you mention the following: "On a second occasion, for instance, when the Serb reservists took Zvornik in Bosnia, the Serb media announced the liberation of the town, not mentioning in a word the several thousands corpses lying in the streets." Tell me, please, where did you get that information from about several thousand bodies in the streets of Zvornik, which is certainly untrue and which you again take as being some sort of undisputed fact. "The Serbian media are not reporting on thousands of bodies in the streets of Zvornik". You know, people are listening to you in Zvornik now, and you can imagine how astonished they will be when they hear that you're claiming there were several thousand bodies in the streets of Zvornik that Serb media did not report about. How could they write about something that didn't happen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just keep your questions shorter and we'll get on more quickly. Mr. de la Brosse, can you find the reference to this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm referring to page 44. That is do you -- are you referring to page 44? Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We haven't got the reference. Give us the reference again so the witness can see it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Footnote 44, and I was quoting from it. It is on page 22, where it says: "They announced the liberation of the town without saying a word about several thousand bodies lying in the streets."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now you're criticising the Serbian press for not writing about something that didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness find the passage. Have you found the passage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've found it. It's footnote 44. The source, as indicated, referring to that event was Florence Hartmann's book, "Milosevic, the diagonal of the madman".

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, you're relying on this as if it were the Bible, and that is an absolutely gross lie which you are using to explain that allegedly Serbian propaganda refuses to report about crimes involving several thousand corpses in the streets of Zvornik. This is what your Florence Hartmann found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. What's the question? The witness has dealt with it. He's given his answer as best he can.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you believe that this answer is acceptable -- well, no, it's a good answer, in fact. He took it from Florence Hartmann's book. You can find even worse things from other propaganda. But this is an absolutely blatant lie. Even the other side knows that. There were no thousands of bodies in the streets of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What's your next question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I have to hurry, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke about the contents of the news published about the killing of Serb children by Croats in Eastern Slavonia. Do you claim that that is not a correct piece of news, the fact that children were killed there?

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you be more specific, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you spoke here orally, you testified orally that some news was put out about the killing of Serb children in Eastern Slavonia, and I'm asking you now, are you saying that it didn't happen and that this was invented by the media, this news item?

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you would look at -- just a moment. Just a moment. Let's find the references. Tab 26 are the references, and there are references in clip 9 of the killing of a child as alleged.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you start out from the fact that all the crimes that the press wrote about were in fact fabricated, invented? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Deal, if you would, with the allegations with regard to children. I've referred you to one at clip 9. There's the reference from "What the Friar Said". I'm also looking for a reference, which at the moment I cannot find, to the allegation that over 40 children were killed. It may be it's in a different -- it may be that it's in a different section.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You were raising these matters, and they must be dealt with, and the witness must have a chance to answer them. There is the reference to the, yes, clip 1 to Serb children being thrown to the lions in the zoo. So it's clip 1, clip 9. And also you may remember there is the reference to the killing of, I think, 41 children. No, I see. It's clip 13. "In Vukovar, more than a thousand Serbs are feared to have been butchered, including several dozen Serbian children who have fallen victim to the Ustasha knives." So those are the three clips which you were -- you referred to. What's being put to you is that, as I understand it, are these facts -- were these facts fabricated or were they true as alleged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As regards the news that 41 Serbian children were murdered by the Ustasha, that information was published and turned out to be false. It was not found, and that's why Reuters press agency itself published a disavowal of that having happened. I think perhaps you were referring to the three examples that I gave. I found the passage. In paragraph 59 of the report where I try to show that through the presentation of individual tragedies, in this case children, allegedly victims of crimes -- that is, Serbian children who were victims of crime committed by other combatants, all of this was to show that, using these three examples, it was -- well, I'm not coming to any conclusions about whether or not this happened. I think that as regards the third example, this is a proven fact. The second refers to the death of the parents of a boy, and the first refers to the death of a boy allegedly killed by Croatian fighters. As regards the first example, I don't know whether the information is correct, but what I wanted to demonstrate through this example is that by showing individual tragedies involving children, the objective was to play on the emotional side of the public by speaking of facts that the viewer would have to have sympathy for, facts for which every protective mechanism on the part of the television viewer would not play. That is when he was talking about the most fragile people, that is children. I'm not saying that the facts alleged or even verified in the three examples didn't -- didn't happen. What I am interested in is the interpretation of the facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. de la Brosse, Mr. de la Brosse, we seem to be losing a lot of time here, but this is an example that cannot serve to anybody's credit. What it says here is this: It says that that killing of children was, first of all, televised by the British television station ITV, and then the media in Serbia televised what went through Reuters. But first, that is to say Reuters, published a denial, a disavowal, and this was cared too, the denial. So the news goes from Reuters. It is transmitted by the media, carried by the media, not only Belgrade but others, and then Reuters publishes a disclaimer. The media carry this, and where do you see Serbian propaganda there? Or perhaps I'd been manipulating with Reuters. You yourself describe what happened, and this is a blatant example of how you in your function of let's call it expertise, of expert testimony, are abusing this kind of material.

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're going back to the example of the master of 41 Serbian children by the Croatian fighters which did not take place. I think we agree on that point. What I said is that the -- the news about that event, which turned out to be incorrect, was widely distributed and used by the Serbian media. The Serb media, once the information had been denied, the Serbian media did not even take the trouble to go and check on it and I put it into the footnote. I say that that information was also denied by the Serbian media except when -- when information is broadcast, information of this type, any disavowal of that information does not set aside the effects that the news originally had created. This can be checked not only in this case in the former Yugoslavia but also with other phenomena of that sort in other countries. So this very strong media coverage of the death of these 41 children supported in the eyes of the public, Serbian public opinion because it was a very broad coverage of that event which was not based on the truth, that strong media -- that very important media coverage supported the image that was cultivated in the Serbian media of a Croatian people which was genocidal and criminal just as that information was used by the media in order to make those opposed to the war be silenced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. de la Brosse, Mr. de la Brosse, I hope it's not being challenged that the media in Serbia carried Reuters reporting and the reporting of ITV. Did Reuters published a disclaimer after that and the media in Serbia disclaimed it too. So they followed these reports put out by Reuters, because the Serbian -- did the Serb media disseminate nationalism because they were carrying a Reuters news item? How can you say such nonsensical things?

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Clarification. This information was spread in the newspapers by those journalists who were there in the former Yugoslavia at the time. The information was distributed by Reuters without having any real on-site checks being made. Other media who were there on the ground did not distribute that information because there were questions about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. de la Brosse. Let's not waste more time on this matter, but I think that this is -- it is illustrative in itself. The facts that you mentioned, information came from Reuters the Serb media carried it, Reuters disclaimed it, the Serbian media disclaimed it and you accuse the Serb media of some sort of propaganda. And to make things quite clear to you, gentlemen, or to make it even more complicated, I have here one of the next witness's --

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't finished answering the question you asked me about. You asked me whether the Serb media had denied that information or disclaimed it. Let me give you an example from Politika which did in fact deny the information through a few lines that were at the back of the newspaper. So it doesn't have the same position in the newspaper as the news had when it was originally put out. And that way it does not erase the effect that had been produced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Disclaimers never deny the effects that the first information has when it's put out. That's a general rule in the media, and I'm sure you ought to know that much better than me. Once you put out a lie, disclaimers never cover that. And for ten years, an enormous mass of lies was put out against Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, let's move on, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Especially --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gentlemen, I have a witness here, he is a Prosecution witness and I have been supplied with this statement. He was on the list and then disappeared from the list but this seems to be common practice with them. Other people seem to crop up all the time. And it doesn't say here that this particular witness is an a protected one but I'm if the going to read out his name because I'm not sure whether he's a protected witness or not. He is a Serb anyway and he is testifying Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. against me, or will be, against me here in this courtroom. And on page 3 and for your purposes, this is 039392, that is the number of the witness statement which was disclosed to me by the other side over there in order to prepare for his testimony. On page 3 of that statement this witness towards the end of paragraph 2 or, rather, this should be paragraph 3, but it's densely typed, says the following: 'On one occasion we found 80 dead Serb children lined up in the hospital. Each of them had a -- three wounds in his back from a bullet shot. I personally saw them, 100 to 150 metres away from the Vukovar Hospital in a ditch. I know they were Serb children because they were identified by the surviving parents," and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You can ask the witness if he's seen that report or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not speaking about -- this is a statement by --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... As far as this witness's evidence is concerned is whether he's seen such a report and he's indicating he hasn't. Whether the witness is called or not, we'll find out. We'll be able to hear his evidence on the point. Yes, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, please, on page 11 and 12, you claim that propaganda becomes detrimental when it is used in a totalitarian fashion, and that is not challenged at all. And when it promotes goals contrary to human and international law. However, what is challenged is the fact that you wish to link this up with the state of affairs in Serbia. My question to you is this: How can you talk about any kind of totalitarianism at that time, not now in Serbia, of course, but at that time in a Serbia in which a multi-party system was in existence, which at that time was introduced, not before but precisely during that period of time a democratically adopted constitution proclaiming guaranteed rights on the basis of international pacts and covenants including secret ballot elections which had a very vociferous and loud opposition, in fact. And every two years there were different extraordinary elections that were held. So how can you, and on the basis of what criteria, can this kind of society be ranked among what you wish to rank Serbia among?

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you indicate the paragraphs that you're referring to, please? You said pages 11, 10 -- 11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's on pages 11, 12. Propaganda --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I be of assistance? It's actually paragraph 12, and it is the last sentence of this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I am referring to in this paragraph through footnote 25 is the message regarding stereotypes whose purpose is to stigmatise other communities. We reviewed the examples last week. I am referring to the distribution of a -- messages fomenting hatred through the regime-controlled media. And in that sense I have based myself on several texts including the covenant on civil and political rights which was ratified by Yugoslavia in 1966 and which requires the Yugoslav state and Serbia to prohibit and to fight against any messages of hatred. And so I note, and perhaps I'm wrong, but I didn't find any traces anywhere whether it be in reports prepared by NGOs or international organisations. I have noted that no activity -- no case was ever brought to a court by the Yugoslav or Serbian authorities against public media which carried out that type of practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me this, Mr. de la Brosse, please, how can you claim -- actually, you're quoting Serbian scientists, for example, with respect to the thesis on creating an unified state in which all Serbs would be living, and you quote the quotations and statements made of Serb scientists, academicians and so on who make no mention of that at all. And the example of this is a quotation from academician Mihajlo Markovic on page 21 and he writes about the tragedy of Serbs under Croatian authority which is ongoing and which in future could even be greater as well as the position of the Serb people in Croatia which is worse than the position of any national minority anywhere, and that is quite right, quite true. Do you know that according to the constitution, pursuant to the Croatian constitution, up until 1990, Croatia was defined as a state of the Serbian people --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Wait a moment. Let the witness deal with this. The reference, as I understand it, is in paragraph 22 to what Mr. Markovic says.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Mr. de la Brosse, have you got the reference?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The reference from the Duga excerpt, is that what your are referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. What's the question, Mr. Milosevic, about this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am referring to the quotation by academician Mihajlo Markovic, and Mr. de la Brosse links this up to with the thesis to create a unified state that would house all the Serbs. Markovic doesn't mention that at all. On page 21 what he does mention is this: He speaks about the tragedy of the Croatian Serbs under Croatian authority which is ongoing and in the future could reach tragic proportions, which unfortunately is quite true. And my question is to you: When you read that, did you know that precisely up until the year 1991 or, rather, in the year 1990 and 1991 the Serb people were thrown out of the Croatian constitution. Up until then Croatia was defined as the Croatian people, the Serb people, and all the peoples living within it. Do you know anything about that at all?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Wait a moment? What's this got to do with anything? What's the point that you're making, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The point I'm making, Mr. May, is in the essence, your own expert, through various quotations, is trying to prove something which does not exist in those quotations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For example --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will take this -- we will take this stage by stage. Just a moment. What is it, first of all, that he's trying to prove?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He wishes to prove that propaganda and that the Serbian Academy of Arts and Sciences worked along the lines of the title of his project that we saw here on the overhead projector, the project of having all Serbs living in one state, state for all Serbs, which isn't written anywhere, which isn't contained in any of the quotations he uses in his text or his footnotes. So it is a complete montage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's the witness answer that. Your proposition is unsupported, it's said, by the quotations from the academicians and others.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite the contrary, in fact. In the quotations which are contained in the footnotes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let him answer one thing at a time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The quotation you're referring to supports paragraph 22 of the report which indicates one of the mechanisms used by the propaganda, that is to put -- to project on others the -- your own fault or your own faults. So the quotation here -- the quotation here is by Mr. Markovic is used as an example. I'm not speaking -- I'm not using the quotation here or relying on it for the purposes that you're alluding to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, your whole work is used for the purposes for which you wrote the report, propaganda as a function of the plan to create a state for all Serbs. Now, how can you separate that and say you're not using it for that purpose? Use a bit of elementary logic, Mr. de la Brosse, please.

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Been asked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This then, please. Do you consider that contrary to the charter on human rights and international law the affirmation of the identity of one's own nation for which you accuse academician Dobrica Cosic, for example, who you claim assumes a special place in the instrumentalisation of Serbian frustrations and the burgeoning of nationalism and that he is directly responsible for the growth of international hatred. That is on page 34, the footnote there.

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me go back to what I was saying a little while ago about the international text that I used and that I quoted talking about unlawful propaganda. I repeat, I based myself on those texts in order to state that at the time, the propaganda of hatred and stigmatisation of a community fell within those international documents that Serbia and Yugoslavia had prescribed to, which had delivered that type of message, that type of hateful message. I'm not saying anything else when I refer to those texts. That's what I mean when I refer to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, then. Please go ahead and quote from those texts, the ones you mention, what you consider to be a message of hatred, because I keep claiming that you are mentioning people and you're quoting quotes in which there is none of what you're claiming. Then there is no message of hate within those quotations. Go ahead, quote. Quote from your text.

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I return to the terminology used in the media which was one of stigmatisation, of denigrating a community or several communities, and in that way I think that I can say - I'm not a legal specialist - but in any case, it seems to me that that type of message of stigmatisation, demonisation of other communities are messages putting forward hatred against a community, and in that way they are covered by international law which Serbia subscribed to. I'm not saying anything more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you've just falsified that, because you cannot quote a single quotation from your footnotes, what you yourself qualify as being a speech of hatred. Otherwise, those listening to this in the Serbian language, let me translate the word stigmatisation. Stigmatisation means to blacken someone, because I keep listening to the word stigmatisation coming from the interpretation. It is to blacken somebody, to demonise them. So please find me an example where somebody is doing that, the Serb media is doing that, that is to say blackening or demonising some other ethnic community.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do that over the adjournment. We're going to adjourn now for 20 minutes. When you come back, Mr. de la Brosse, you can answer that question with a passage. Yes, 20 minutes. Before we call the next witness, there are matters under Rule 92 bis on which rulings are required. Perhaps I could give everybody warning that we will discuss these. They relate to the statements of witnesses B-1455, 1775, and also the transcripts of Mr. Selak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I only received 1455 and 1775, I think it is, on Friday. I've been able to consider 1455 but not 1775 yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, perhaps we can have a discussion about it anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We will adjourn now, 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. de la Brosse, you were asked before the adjournment about any speech which might be described as a speech of hatred, and it was put to you that you couldn't yourself quote from your footnotes any such speech. Now, you should have the opportunity of answering that. Perhaps you could do so briefly. But if there is any particular speech you have in mind you can, of course, refer us to it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would recall that in some of the clips that were shown last week, I referred to footnote 147 and 146. There we can see that through the terminology used, speaking about Ustasha, what is shown is a group through the use of terminology which will stigmatise it. As regards the quotations in the report and on which I based myself, I should refer you to footnote 85 in my report. In footnote 85, and you see all of the quotations which refer to the mechanism which would be used against the Croats who are presented as the heirs of those responsible for the crimes committed against other populations, including the Serbs, during the Second World War. Through the quotations which I use to support myself, we see a historical amalgamation whose purpose is to use different types of quotations with terms that are used. Perhaps we could look at the various quotations which come from Politika in which one describes a direct link between the Croatian government in 1990 and the-- rather, the Croatian community and the Croatian government of the Second World War. And so what connection is drawn between the crimes committed by the Second World War Croatian government and the crimes and activities of the Franjo Tudjman government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. I think we've got 85 in front of us, and we can see what's set out there. Now, Mr. Milosevic, you've got ten minutes left for questioning of this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is not sufficient for me, Mr. May, ten minutes. Would you please consider the possibility of giving me a little more time with this witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You can have another half hour starting from now. So you can have until half past eleven.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough, as you say that you mention certain quotations, in any of those quotations is a nation being stigmatised or denigrated. You mention authorities committing crimes against the Serbs, who have thrown the Serbs from the constitution, who have fired the Serbs from all public services, who are persecuting the Serbs in an organised manner. Find me a single quotation in which the nation as such is being denigrated, be it the Croats or the Albanians where the Croats are being stigmatised or the Albanians being stigmatised as a national minority. That was my question to you.

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In footnote 85, the second quotation, an express connection is made here. Should I read it in English? [In English] "Democratic community is proud of Ante Starcevic according to folk saying" -- "is proud of Ante Starcevic, according to folk saying, the words, shy away from places where the fools treat -- treat. Croatia is proud of so-called independent state and is covertly and stealthily priming the new slaughter of Serbs in Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina." [Interpretation] So what is described here is Croatia as a whole, something that includes all of the population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. de la Brosse --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let him finish. Yes, Mr. de la Brosse, is there something you want to add?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A generalisation is made about the entire Croatian people. I would also like to quote or, rather, to recall the video clip. I don't remember the number, but the transcript of the Jovan Raskovic's statement is found in footnote 117, in paragraph 54. It follows a statement of Dobrica Cosic which was -- we've also had the opportunity to see at the beginning of my testimony. Through those two examples a constant reminder is made in respect of the atrocities committed by the independent Croatian state under the Ustasha and the attentions ascribed to Franjo Tudjman's regime. If I read the excerpt which appeared -- the excerpt from Jovan Raskovic which appeared in Serbian television, I would remind you that he is speaking about the fact that genocide has begun and it depends on the Serbs in Croatia and in Serbia and the international factor, Europe and the world whether their movement [In English] "open its concentration camps, pits used as collective tombs. But one thing is for sure, Serbs will never again be led to the pits by just the Ustasha. Serbs have to put up a great resistance and the genocidal idea will collapse along with the genocidal Croatian state." [Interpretation] I would recall that Jovan Raskovic, who was the promoter of this idea according to which the Croatian people had a -- has a genocidal character. I would also like to quote another example of this type of amalgamation which was made by certain Serbian intellectuals. The example is in a -- is in a statement by Jovan Raskovic that you can find on the 25th of March, 1990, in Politika. This is an example that I didn't use in the report. It isn't quoted as such, but I can give you the quotation which is in English. "[In English] That that which disrupts relations between Serbs and Croats now is connected to the genocide which was perpetrated against the Serbian people by the Croatian Ustasha regime. We can conclude that this hiding of genocide, this hiding of genocide represents an appeal for -- to history -- for history," excuse me, "for a repeat." [Interpretation] The second quotation that I'd like to give to you in order to replace things in their proper context is also an excerpt from Politika of the 7th of August, 1992, in which Radovan Samardzic states that: "[Previous translation continues]... [In English] Who are constantly exposed to genocide. The Serbs are the people that." Through these various examples of historical amalgamation between two situations which are not the same, what is shown is the Croatian regime and the Croatian people at the beginning of the 1990s as the heirs of the Croatian government of the Second World War. And as such, I might be wrong but I think that a stereotype is being presented and what is sought is the demonisation of a community by relying on historic amalgamations which remain to be proved.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. de la Brosse, you give very lengthy answers so that half an hour will really not be sufficient if you continue in that way. So would you please be kind enough to bear in mind what you yourself said. You said that the expression is that the Croatian Democratic Union and then you come to the conclusion that the reference is to the whole people. The HDZ, the Croatian Democratic Union, was the party which in restarted the persecution of the Serbs 50 years later, not the Croatian people. The HDZ is not the Croatian people. Therefore, in what you yourself have said, you say the authorities, then you make a comma, and then you add the Croatian people yourself, which no one has referred to. So you're making -- you're construing something that could be described as a forgery. Now, did you perhaps have occasion to see -- I have shown here a film, though very briefly as my time is extremely limited, an extract of what Simon Wiesenthal said in connection with those crimes? Can you imagine that Simon Wiesenthal was also in the service of the national list objectives that the Serbian leadership led by me was implementing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is the question? There's one about the HDZ which we will allow the witness to answer, but what's the second question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The second question which is linked to what I just mentioned:

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your second paragraph on page 43, paragraph 47, you describe as a manipulation the fact that in the media there was reference to the genocide committed by the NDH against the Serbian people during the Second World War. The word "genocide" in your text is in quotation marks, and you're suggesting by doing so that it never took place, the NDH being the Independent State of Croatia. On pages 52 and 53 again, you are criticising reference to the crimes of the NDH suggesting that they were exaggerating. Do you know that according to official data of the former Yugoslavia that was headed by Tito, who was a Croat, about 700.000 Serbs, Romanies and Jews were killed in the Jasenovac concentration camps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's another question. So there are two questions there for you, Mr. de la Brosse. Just a moment. Just a moment, please. Let him answer. The first question is you are -- let him answer what you're Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. putting. The first question is that you are conflating in some way the HDZ with the Croatian people and ascribing to the Croatian people what was purely ascribed to the HDZ. What would your answer be to that? If you could briefly answer that, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I quoted Mr. Jovan Raskovic on several occasions. What he says has to be related to the way that he -- that he writes and speaks. Let me remind you that in work that I do quote in a footnote, Jovan Raskovic describes the Croatian people as having a genocidal nature. The fact that through statements that he made in the press and to which I have just given -- which I've just read out to you, one should recall that Jovan Raskovic was invited to all the television programmes on Serbian television at the time wherever he was able to put forward, to explain his theory according to which the Croatian people had a genocidal nature. Therefore, in the public's eyes, the connection was made. The example which I read out a little while ago I believe makes use of that conflation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. I think really we must move on. The second question or the second point which is made is that you have been playing down the genocide, as it's put, during the Second World War. Is that right or not? Have you been playing that down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. Absolutely not. I want to be very clear about that. If I put it into quotation marks, the word "genocide" in quotation marks, because even historians raise that question, because there is not an agreement about the extent of the number of the victims of that genocide. So to -- using the word "genocide" was referring to that historical uncertainty, not the fact that the massacre took place but what the extent of the massacre was. It's in no way a denial of the genocide.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Since you're doing the same thing as the new Croatian regime did after the elections, that is minimising the genocide, here is what the Wiesenthal centre says. In the Wiesenthal centre, and you can find this, you can take the Internet and search for it. "Jasenovac was the largest camp in Croatia [In English] between 1941 and 1945 under department 3 of the Croatian security police. About 600.000 people were murdered here, Serbs, Jewish, [Interpretation] In brackets 30.000 of them, Gypsies and opponents of the Ustasha regime." So you are claiming that the figures don't match and that this is something in dispute in your opinion, but for the Wiesenthal centre, it is not in dispute. You will also be able to find his definition of the concept of Ustasha and the Wiesenthal centre says and I quote again: "Created in 1930 [In English] Was a Croatian national terrorist organisation. Its members [Interpretation] Ustasha was a Croatian terrorist organisation. Its member's hatred of the Jews was only rivalled by their hatred of the Serbs. [In English] Power of the Hitler created a Croatian puppet state. In 1941 Ustasha terrorists killed 500.000 Serbs, expelled 250.000 and forced 250.000 to convert to Catholicism. They murdered thousands of Jewish and Gypsies." [Interpretation] Are you aware of these facts? Can't you see that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let him answer. Let him answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To be very clear, I'm not denying that hundreds of thousands of Serbs and other peoples were massacred, massacred in the camps. What I'm simply trying to say is that since I'm not an historian, I saw the various estimates in respect of the various numbers of deaths which would -- and they weren't the same in all the different articles, but there was a spread from 500 to 900.000. Since I'm not an historian, since I see there is no absolute consensus on the specific number of deaths in those Croatian camps, I thought that it would be more prudent to put in the quotations around the word "genocide." If that was understood differently, I am sorry, but that was my intention as a person who is not an historian. I wanted to show caution in this area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. de la Brosse, perhaps your report would have been strengthened in this respect if the explanation that you just gave had been inserted either as a footnote or indeed in the text, the explanation, that is, as to why you have "genocide" in quotation marks.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I move on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. I'd like the witness to comment on that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I should have indicated that in a footnote. It is true that when I prepared the report my objective was to describe the propaganda mechanisms, and it is true that I was not aware of the need or of the significance there would be in dealing with certain historical facts about which I did not feel qualified, and for that reason, that might have been something clumsy on my part. If I were to redo this work, I would include a footnote that I was led by caution, perhaps in a clumsy way, to explain why I put quotations around that word and not being an historian, and I could not come to a specific decision about a factual issue that -- an issue dealing with facts that had occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And I will prove to you now that this reference to your lack of qualifications is not correct and that, in fact, it testifies to your lack of objectivity. In footnote 119, you quote the sorrowful comments by Florence Hartmann because the parallel showing of Franjo Tudjman and Ante Pavelic's speeches - and Ante Pavelic headed this puppet state in 1941 - in a TV programme on the 27th of July 1991. So my question to you is: Are you aware that Tudjman in those quoted speeches said something that Pavelic also said, namely do you know that at the rally of the HDZ held on the 24th and 25th of February, 1990 in Zagreb, the then-elected president of that newly formed party, Tudjman, said among other things and I quote: "The Independent State of Croatia," and he's referring to the Pavelic state, "was not only a quisling entity and a fascist crime but also an expression of the historic aspirations of the Croatian people." End of quotation. Therefore, you say that you are uninformed, that you are not an historian, but the lament of Florence Hartmann regarding the link between Tudjman and Pavelic you find necessary to quote. But as you see, the link is quite obvious and quite clear. What would be your comment to that, Mr. de la Brosse?

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I quoted that excerpt from a work by Florence Hartmann, it has to do with the fact that she also shows, with examples, what the amalgamation was that was made between those responsible for the genocide and massacres committed by the Croats during the Second World War and what Franjo Tudjman was prepared -- was preparing to do allegedly. I didn't read the work that you're referring to by Franjo Tudjman. If I used this quotation, it is because the constant recalling of the past - constant - and the comparison made between the Croatian government of 1990 and that in the Second World War, in the readers' minds and the television viewer's mind, what is created is a type of confusion, because what -- what is-- message is that as the regime is on the point of -- of repeating the massacres, the massacres that were committed by the Ustashas during the Second World War. And the quotation which I gave you a little while ago by Jovan Raskovic in Politika, the 25th of March, 1990, is, in my opinion, something which sheds light on what we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you find that is the justification for this. But the link, as you can see from the quotation, was made by Tudjman himself, because he says that that entity was the historic expression of the aspirations of the Croatian people. So it was not the Belgrade press that made this link but he himself. Isn't that right or not?

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't read that work by Tudjman that you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I said it was his speech at a Congress of the HDZ which you should have read if you're denying this link with -- which he himself made in that same speech.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We have it. We have the point, Mr. Milosevic, insofar as there is one. You said Tudjman referred in a speech in 1990 to the NDH government and said it represented the aspirations of the people of Croatia. The witness is saying to you that the constant repetition of these wrongs in the 1990s, the constant repetition of this was a way of building up hatred and a way of justifying the use of force and violence. That's his evidence. What the significance is of it will be a matter for us. Now, there is not much point going on arguing about what Mr. Tudjman may or may not have said.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe he didn't say it. Very well. He may not have said it. And maybe he did not make this link. Then we're okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But tell me, please, how do you, as a media expert, because you keep referring to this amalgamation, and obviously there's an amalgamation between you and Florence Hartmann, between you and this illegal OTP and not the way you put it. How can you, as an expert for the media, who doesn't know the language which the media use, in paragraph 52, second paragraph on page 49, when the TV was the only source of information for more than 90 per cent of the Serbs in confirmation of that in footnote 107, you quote from an article by Nicole du Roy, who with a very moderate title, "Serbia Paranoiac Television," et cetera, you have the references there, and the quotation is: In this country Serbia where 46 per cent of the people are illiterate, which would mean every other inhabitant, the only form of media information which covers the whole territory are information broadcast by state television." It seems to me, Mr. de la Brosse, that even you who upon the instructions of the opposite side prepared this report, this is going a little too far in saying that in Serbia 46 per cent of the people are illiterate. People are watching in Serbia and probably they can't believe their own ears, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, this will be your last question, because you've now gone on for half an hour. Yes. But you can finish it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But those are your sources, Mr. de la Brosse. Forty-six per cent of the people in Serbia are illiterate.

utterances.speaker: RENAUD DE LA BROSSE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that you're confusing illiteracy and people who haven't studied. Here we are speaking of people whose only diploma would be from primary school. We're not talking about people who can't read and write at all. Reading -- that's not the same thing. People who have limited education and those who are illiterate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is a very lame excuse. A little later in the report, you say that state television, at the end of page 90, 91, paragraph 110, you say that state television and I quote now: "For 30 per cent of the population who have not completed elementary school was the only and exclusive source of information." So now you are referring to those who not completed eight years of elementary school. Earlier on it was four years, and it was increased to eight years.
